title: A client supplies the ownership relation at invocation time
coversRequirement: AZ7 required behaviour — clients and Apps cannot supply an ownership relation at invocation time
target: AZ7 / runtime enforcement of own scope
why: The ownership relation is declared once, in the manifest, and resolved by the platform from the authenticated context. A caller that can name the owner it is scoped to can name any owner, which turns 'own' from a restriction into a parameter and defeats it entirely — the same class of defect as taking tenant identity from a client-supplied field. The extra fields here must be REFUSED, not ignored: a silently dropped field looks to the caller like it was honoured, and to a reviewer like the API accepts it.
notes: RUNTIME OBLIGATION. NOT DECIDABLE BY app-manifest.schema.json AT ALL — the manifest is the declaration, this is an invocation against it, and no manifest fixture can test it. NOT YET EXECUTABLE: no invocation contract or request-envelope schema exists in packages/contracts/**, and no test framework is approved (TESTING_STANDARD.md open question TS1), so this case is a SPECIFICATION carried in the fixture set so the obligation is not lost, NOT a passing test. Report it as NOT RUN until an invocation contract exists. When it does exist, the enforcement point is Core: AUTHORIZATION_STANDARD.md requires the scope be evaluated server-side on every call, so the check belongs alongside tenant resolution and not in the App or the SDK.

invocation.attack: The caller supplies both a value for the ownership field ('created_by') naming a DIFFERENT principal, and a redefinition of which field carries ownership ('ownershipField': 'label'). Either one, if honoured, lets principal-alpha-1 act on records owned by principal-alpha-2.

mustNot: silently ignore the extra fields and proceed
use the client-supplied created_by value in the ownership predicate
use the client-supplied ownershipField name in place of the declared one
leak whether principal-alpha-2 or widget-synthetic-0001 exists
requiredOutcome.mustAlso: The ownership predicate is built from the manifest declaration and the authenticated principal only.
